# OrgMod — Modernization {.unnumbered}

**OrgMod** is the modernization member of the Org family — the operational
expression of the UIAO substrate that moves a legacy estate forward *without
rip-and-replace*. Its core is vendor-neutral: adapter interfaces for
directory, device, PKI, RADIUS, DNS/DHCP/IPAM, and overlay-adjacent control
surfaces, driven by an assessment engine, a defined target surface, and
program management that keeps the whole journey change-controlled. Active
Directory → Entra ID remains the leading worked path, but OrgMod is designed
to govern heterogeneous stacks beyond that single journey.

**OrgPath** governs, **OrgComp** proves federal organizational compliance,
**OrgMod** modernizes — three expressions of one substrate, adoptable
together or entirely independently.

## What OrgMod modernizes

- **The assessment engine** — enumerate what the legacy estate actually does
  before deciding what replaces it; the
  [modernization program](../customer-documents/operational-guides/uiao-modernization-program/index.qmd)
  carries the engine, target surface, and program-management discipline.
- **The target surface** — [Intune policy templates](../customer-documents/operational-guides/target-surface/intune-policy-templates.qmd),
  the [Conditional Access library](../customer-documents/operational-guides/access-plane/conditional-access-library.qmd),
  and the cross-adapter [modernization specs](../customer-documents/modernization-specs/index.qmd).
- **A worked consumer** — the
  [SQL Server Identity Transformation](../customer-documents/sql-server-narrative/index.qmd)
  series migrates a twenty-year SQL estate off Windows Authentication onto
  Entra ID, end to end.
- **The long-form argument** — the modernization tracks of the
  [whitepaper reading guide](../customer-documents/whitepapers/reading-guide.qmd):
  Track 2 carries the AD → Entra ID arc from
  [the structural migration problem](../customer-documents/whitepapers/ad-to-entraid-migration-problem.qmd)
  through
  [flipping 50,000 devices to hybrid join](../customer-documents/whitepapers/hybrid-join-without-governance.qmd),
  and Track 4 carries the network and infrastructure decisions — transport
  under TIC 3.0, DNS in the hybrid multi-cloud, and the field-office WAN
  case. These ship in the OrgMod kit's `Whitepapers/` folder.
- **The seams to its siblings** — OrgMod's changes land on the addressing
  plane OrgPath governs, and the evidence they produce is what OrgComp
  proves; adopt any of the three alone, or all together. What OrgMod does
  *not* carry is steady-state governance operations: the Active Governance
  Directory, federal AI identity governance, and the Help Desk / Cloud
  Services authority model sit in the same `operational-guides/` tree but
  are [OrgPath's](../orgpath/index.qmd), because their deliverable is an
  estate governed rather than an estate moved.

## One lifecycle, three pillars {#macdr}

Every operational change the Org family touches — every **Move, Add, Change,
Deletion, and Reset (MACD-R)** — travels the same five-clause authorized
path: **it originates with the SSOT → carries an authoritative authorization
→ executes under least privilege with just-in-time elevation (PIM) → closes
with provenance → emits verified, secured evidence automatically to
continuous monitoring.** OrgMod applies the law at migration scale: a wave
is a batch of Moves originated by the modernization plan's source of truth,
each executed under a just-in-time role and each emitting per-object
closure evidence — which is how a migration stays an audited operation
instead of a weekend of standing admin rights. The non-human classes OrgMod
moves have designated SSOTs of their own: devices originate in the
asset-lifecycle registry (MDM enrollment is enforcement, not truth),
declared infrastructure originates in the IaC repository, and every item
migrated must carry a human owner resolvable in the HR SSOT — an ownerless
item is an orphan finding before it is a migration candidate. The full
doctrine — including Closure Provenance ("no closure counts unless it
carries its proof") and the per-class
[SSOT Registry](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd#ssot-registry)
— is stated in
[OrgComp Vol 0 Book 00](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd#macdr-lifecycle).

## Narrative provenance — the modernization arc mapped to canon

The forty-year mainframe-to-cloud arc circulates as the standalone whitepaper
[Modernization Journey](../customer-documents/whitepapers/modernization-journey.qmd),
which is deliberately vendor- and product-neutral: it cites only NIST, OMB,
CISA and FedRAMP, and carries no UIAO claims, so it can be handed to an agency
that is not evaluating a platform. It also circulates as
[OrgComp Vol I Book 05](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_I_Book_05_OrgComp_Network_Modernization.qmd),
which carries the federal control-closure framing and the SD-WAN / INR
implementation appendix — and which, as part of a series an agency must be able
to adopt without hearing about any automation engine, names no engine either.

Neither of those may carry the canon trail, so **this hub is its canonical
home.** Below is the line-by-line provenance for the arc's fourth act,
including where earlier framings were corrected to match canon.

| Narrative claim | Canon anchor | Reconciliation note |
|---|---|---|
| Separate truth from runtime enforcement; AD conflated directory + DC | [ADR-092 §1](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-092-active-governance.md) | Verbatim doctrine; the spine of Act 4. |
| OrgPath restores addressable truth | [UIAO_151](../../src/uiao/canon/UIAO_151_OrgPath_Codebook.md), [ADR-092 §2](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-092-active-governance.md) | **Corrected:** OrgPath is an *addressing attribute every object carries*, not a "governance primitive," and **not** "every token includes an OrgPath." Decisions *compose against* it. |
| Application-aware networking; token-bound per-call transport | [ADR-066](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-066-application-aware-networking-and-token-bound-transport.md) | Proposed (amended by ADR-123); generalized by accepted ADR-092. "Session is no longer a canonical concept." |
| Vendor products (SD-WAN platform, cloud on-ramp) | [ADR-092 §2](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-092-active-governance.md), [Book_17](../customer-documents/orgpath-narrative/Book_17.qmd) | **Softened:** canon names a neutral `sdwan-fabric` slot, Azure Policy, ISE/ClearPass/Entra RADIUS. Specific platforms are illustrative, incorporated as providers. |
| Session→token identity; CBA replaces Kerberos | [ADR-068](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-068-kerberos-ntlm-elimination.md), [ADR-004](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-004-workload-identity-federation-default.md) | Canonical. NTLM elimination + CBA + Cloud Kerberos trust. |
| Active Governance; L0–L4 ladder; federal L3 ceiling | [ADR-092 §3–4](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-092-active-governance.md) | Verbatim; the keystone of the way forward. |
| Restore single source of truth / provenance | [ADR-074](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-074-drift-ssot-contention.md), [ADR-040](../../src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-040-drift-engine.md) | Canonical, framed as **governance / accountability / integrity**. Program-integrity stakes are the agency's real-world motivation, not a UIAO canon claim. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Provenance

Acts 1–3 of the narrative are a synthesis of an agency modernization arc
(mainframe → regional decentralization → security-layer accretion →
multi-cloud breaking point); the specific institutional details (twelve
regional domains, the named data-center anchors) are the agency's own and are
not asserted as UIAO canon. Act 4 is reconciled to canon as tabulated above.
Mapping first staged 2026-06-04 inside the whitepaper; moved here on
2026-09-09, when that paper's two editions were consolidated into one
vendor-neutral edition with no canon references left in it.
:::
